newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singaporeans are not swept off feet by WTO meet.
newsitem.headline: Singaporeans are not swept off feet by WTO meet.

text.p: It may be the biggest international event Singapore has ever hosted, but residents of the city-state are not too impressed by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting.
"It is a good thing. It has put Singapore on the world map but I don't think anything is going to come out of this," said Jean Sit, assistant marketing manager at the Suntec City convention centre.
"It is a bit 'sikit atas' (over the top). I don't think Joe Blow in the street is interested in this," said an oil trader at a European firm.
Few of the republic's three million people seem to be keeping tabs on the proceedings.
"I haven't actually read anything exciting that's come out of the WTO at all," said Mark Falconer, sales desk manager at NatWest Futures.
"There'll be no market-moving news out of it so we're ignoring all the headlines."
The WTO meeting started on Monday and has since been the scene of intense negotiations over various trade issues.
Most of the 2,800 delegates and 1,600 journalists crowding the huge Suntec convention centre are bleary-eyed after days and nights of parlays over arcane trade terms.

Things have been hardly less intense on Boat Quay, where young Singaporeans and foreign exchange traders gather nightly to have a blast in a row of pubs and karaoke bars strung alongside the Singapore river.
Some people hope to see one concrete result from the WTO -- cheaper telephone bills.
Singapore Telecoms' monopoly will end in March 2000, seven years ahead of the target date, in a laissez-faire gesture from the hosts.
